correctness.rationale: Derivation is exact for all odd a,b≥3 and 1≤s<min(a,b): after first effective update the other edge alone may remain active; after its firing private colors are fixed, and each private block dominates all shared flips iff 2s is strictly smaller than its full edge size. This gives a deterministic two-state recurrent class or consensus in at most four effective updates. Uniform earliest active clocks yield conditional formula; accounting for initially inactive other group yields unbiased law (T_a+T_b)/2. The standalone checker independently confirms 18,544 statewise rational comparisons and 46 fair-average comparisons. Finite tests do not establish universal proof.

originality.rationale: The pre-existing 3-uniform loose-hyperstar analysis fixes two triplets to one shared vertex; that yields the (3,3,1) probability 1/4 and is not claimed as new. The new result gives all pairs of odd group sizes, every allowable shared intersection, exact arbitrary-initial-state absorption probabilities, an if-and-only-if overlap threshold, and the explicit unbiased binomial-tail law. Relevant accessible full-text source results on more general hypergraph dynamics were compared for coverage, not only by title. No directly dominating theorem was found, though unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: The two overlapping social groups form the smallest structurally nontrivial finite majority interaction system. The all-size conditional and exact ex-ante law, and if-and-only-if overlap threshold, quantify when shared members do and do not enforce global agreement. The result is a natural complete classification and supplies clear boundary cases for sparse higher-order contagion and opinion models, beyond the known triplet single-overlap special case.
